channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ministry of Sports Holds Dialogue with 15,000 Coaches
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Sports hosted an unprecedented open dialogue with 15,000 coaches and specialists from across the country. Discussions covered the current state of sports, coach challenges, and proposals for future development. New initiatives include improving sports school management and streamlining athlete ranking processes.

item.title: Seattle Mayor Declares September 1st 'Uzbekistan Independence Day'
item.description: The Mayor of Seattle has officially declared September 1, 2026, as 'Uzbekistan Independence Day.' The proclamation highlights Uzbekistan's strengthened sovereignty, sustainable development, and reforms since independence. It also notes the country's strategic location and potential for trade and investment with Seattle.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches 163 New Projects Ahead of 35th Independence Anniversary
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched 163 new projects in anticipation of its 35th Independence Day. These initiatives are part of ongoing reforms aimed at modernizing the economy, improving governance, and fostering business and investment. Key reforms include currency liberalization and reduced tax burdens.

item.title: EAEU goods traceability system to launch September 1
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Tax Service announces the launch of a goods traceability system within the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) on September 1. This system aims to control the circulation of specific goods, including refrigerators, washing machines, and televisions. The mandatory use of electronic waybills will be canceled for these items.

item.title: Bishkek imposes construction work restrictions due to SCO and World Nomad Games
item.description: Bishkek has temporarily restricted construction work and the use of heavy machinery for three days starting August 30. The measures are intended to ensure security and public order during the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit and the World Nomad Games. Energy sector officials urge caution near power facilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank aims to increase local currency financing
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to gradually increase local currency financing and focus more on direct foreign investment rather than external debt, according to Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov. This shift aims to mitigate currency risks historically associated with foreign currency borrowing. The market for soum-denominated financing is developing, with companies now issuing Eurobonds in national currency.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Sets Goal to Reach $300 Billion Economy by 2030
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced a new goal to increase Uzbekistan's economy to $300 billion by 2030. He stated that the next decade will be a period of national growth, achievable through the nation's intellect, labor, and unity. The government plans seven national programs, focusing on education, healthcare, and high-tech economic models.

item.title: Nepal Floods Death Toll Rises to 538, with 977 Missing
item.description: The death toll from floods in Nepal has reached 538, with 977 people reported missing, according to the National Emergency Operation Center. Among the missing are 517 foreign nationals. The floods, triggered by a landslide on the Nepal-Tibet border, have destroyed homes, roads, and infrastructure. China reported five deaths and 558 missing in Tibet.

item.title: Azerbaijan presents tourism potential in Tashkent to boost bilateral cooperation
item.description: Azerbaijan's Tourism Bureau held a presentation in Tashkent showcasing the country's tourism potential to enhance cooperation with Uzbekistan. The event gathered tourism businesses from both nations, focusing on strengthening ties, sharing experiences, and promoting Azerbaijan as a year-round destination.

item.title: Trial for Kyrgyz citizen detained in Turkey set for September 9
item.description: The trial for Kyrgyz citizen Ermek Sabirzhanov, detained in Turkey on suspicion of links to the "Hizmet" movement, is scheduled for September 9 in Izmir. Sabirzhanov is currently held in Sincan prison in Ankara. He was arrested on May 22 at Ankara's Esenboğa Airport while traveling with his family. Turkish authorities accuse him of ties to FETO.

item.title: Uzbek President meets Singapore's Senior Minister, discusses investment and partnership
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong to discuss strengthening bilateral relations. They noted dynamic growth in trade and joint ventures, with Singaporean investments reaching $2 billion. Plans were agreed to expand investment and develop strategic partnership programs.

item.title: Uzbekistan aims to attract foreign investment as a single region: Timur Ishmetov
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to diversify sources of foreign direct investment and avoid dependence on a single region or country, stated Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov in an interview with the Financial Times. While China is a major partner, Uzbekistan is strengthening ties with Europe and the US. The goal is to maintain good relations with many countries.

item.title: International Investment Forum Opens in Syrdarya Region, Uzbekistan
item.description: An international investment forum, "Do Business in Syrdarya!", has commenced in Syrdarya, Uzbekistan. The two-day event aims to showcase the region's investment potential to international businesses, foster new partnerships, and sign mutually beneficial agreements. Over 300 foreign investors from 20 countries are participating.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Committee Discusses Factors for Sustainable Economic Growth
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate Committee on Budget and Economic Issues discussed measures and results related to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) month. Committee Chairman Erkin Gadoyev highlighted that SDGs are linked to state budget parameters and social spending, with significant funds allocated to poverty reduction, education, and healthcare.

item.title: UNEP: Global Lake Pollution Could More Than Double by Mid-Century
item.description: The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) warns that global lake pollution may more than double by mid-century. Lakes, crucial for freshwater supply and biodiversity, are under-resourced, especially in developing nations. Pollution from fertilizers, pesticides, and industrial waste degrades water quality and habitats.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Liberalize Water and Utility Tariffs, Central Bank Head Says
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to complete the liberalization of tariffs for water and other communal services currently regulated administratively. Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov told Financial Times that this process, alongside currency and energy reforms, contributed to inflation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allows State to Buy Shares of Systemically Important Banks Facing Collapse
item.description: Starting September 6, the government or a national holding company can acquire shares of systemically important banks at risk of collapse using state funds. The National Bank and the Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market have approved the procedure for such intervention.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Fully Independent in Monetary Policy Decisions, Says Chairman
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank is fully independent in making key interest rate decisions and conducting monetary policy, according to Chairman Timur Ishmetov in an interview with Financial Times. He stated the bank faces no government pressure in its decisions.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Lays Wreath at Monument of Independence
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited "New Uzbekistan" park and laid a wreath at the Monument of Independence. The monument reflects the nation's history, scholars, commanders, and significant events. The ceremony was held on the occasion of the 35th anniversary of the country's independence.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tightens Energy Audit Requirements for Businesses
item.description: Starting September 6, Kazakh businesses must more accurately calculate energy consumption per unit of production. Audits will include measurements in winter and summer, and assessments of modernization benefits. "Eyeballing" savings is prohibited; calculations must be supported by measurements and technical data.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Remittances Exceed $1.5 Billion in First Half of 2026
item.description: Remittances to Kyrgyzstan reached $1.54 billion in the first half of 2026, with net inflows totaling $1.39 billion, according to the National Bank. June saw peak inflows of $292.1 million. CIS countries remain the primary source, accounting for over 92% of inflows. Migrant remittances support domestic demand and the Kyrgyz som.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Prepares Roadmap for Capital Account Liberalization
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank is preparing a roadmap to further liberalize capital account operations, with the document currently undergoing inter-agency approval. Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov told the Financial Times that the next phase of reforms will involve gradually expanding capital movement freedom after liberalizing the foreign exchange market and allowing freer exchange rate formation.

item.title: Police Lieutenant Colonel Sentenced in Jambyl Region for Bribery
item.description: A deputy head of the Bayzak district police department in the Jambyl region, Lieutenant Colonel Talgat Sarsenov, has been found guilty of accepting a bribe. The court sentenced him to a fine of nine million tenge for promising to close a criminal case in exchange for 300,000 tenge. He was detained on July 31.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan received over $1.5 billion in remittances in first half of 2026
item.description: In the first half of 2026, Kyrgyzstan received $1.539 billion in remittances. Capital outflow reached $150.6 million, resulting in a net inflow of $1.388 billion, according to the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic. Remittances peaked in June 2026, with CIS countries being the primary source.

item.title: Almaty residents protest new general plan, citing developer interests
item.description: Residents of low-rise districts in Almaty are protesting the city's new general plan, arguing it prioritizes developers over citizens. They claim the plan was rushed and approved with procedural violations. Concerns include rezoning of private sector areas for high-rise construction, potentially displacing residents and increasing city risks.

item.title: Aybek Dadebay elected Speaker of Kazakhstan's Qurultay
item.description: Aybek Dadebay, former head of the Presidential Administration and leader of the 'Adilet' party, has been elected Speaker of Kazakhstan's new unicameral parliament, the Qurultay. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev nominated Dadebay, citing his extensive experience in public administration and patriotism.

item.title: Central Bank issues gold and silver coins commemorating 35 years of independence
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has issued commemorative gold and silver coins dedicated to the 35th anniversary of the country's independence. Sales began on August 27 at 690 commercial bank branches. The collection features three coins united by a concept reflecting national statehood, historical heritage, and modern development.

item.title: Aibek Dadebay Elected Speaker of Kazakhstan's New Parliament
item.description: Aibek Dadebay has been elected Speaker of Kazakhstan's new Parliament. Deputies of the Kurultai unanimously supported his candidacy in a secret ballot. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev had previously nominated Dadebay, who was the leader of the Adilet party and former presidential chief of staff.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Germany enhance cooperation in state real estate management
item.description: An online seminar was held between Uzbekistan's State Assets Management Agency and German federal bodies to discuss state real estate management. Participants focused on Germany's experience, modern management mechanisms, and practical experience exchange. Cooperation in this sphere began in 2009, with Germany's BImA agency noted for its transparent evaluation and rental processes.

item.title: Bishkek Emergency Medical Center to Maintain Full Operations During SCO and WCG Events
item.description: The Bishkek Center for Emergency Medicine will operate normally during the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and VI World Nomad Games events, ensuring emergency medical care for residents. The center has enhanced its operations, developed a medical support plan, and strategically deployed teams to minimize response times amid potential traffic restrictions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Pay Interviewers 15,000 Som for Statistical Surveys Starting September 2026
item.description: Interviewers conducting household surveys for Kyrgyzstan's National Statistical Committee will receive a compensatory payment of 15,000 som. The payment, proportional to time worked, will not affect vacation pay or social benefits. This decision by the cabinet of ministers takes effect on September 1, 2026.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Two transport inspectors hired with fake diplomas
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's transport prosecutor's office uncovered two individuals employed at the Issyk-Kul transport control department using falsified higher education diplomas. The accused presented diplomas from local universities, but investigations confirmed they never attended these institutions. Two criminal cases for document forgery have been initiated.

item.title: Kazakhstan's KazMunayGas raises record 3.5 billion yuan in Asian capital markets
item.description: KazMunayGas (KMG) is set to raise 3.5 billion yuan in Asian capital markets, attracting over 25 billion yuan in investor demand. Moody's assigned an investment-grade rating of Baa1 to the bonds. The issuance includes five-year bonds at 2.3% coupon and ten-year bonds at 2.8%.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Singapore discuss strategic partnership and innovation program
item.description: Uzbekistan and Singapore are discussing the development of a medium-term joint program on strategic and innovative partnership, focusing on trade, investment, technology transfer, public administration modernization, human capital development, and digitalization. The discussion occurred during a meeting between President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong.

item.title: Kyrgyz President offers condolences to China over Tibet mudslide disaster
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov sent condolences to Chinese President Xi Jinping following a deadly mudslide in Tibet. The disaster resulted in deaths and numerous missing persons, including foreign nationals. Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Ministry confirmed no Kyrgyz citizens were among the victims.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Africa to establish preferential trade agreement
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Africa have agreed to begin work on a preferential trade agreement. The issue was discussed during a video conference between Uzbekistan's Minister of Investments, Industry, and Trade, Laziz Kudratov, and South Africa's Minister of Trade, Industry, and Competition, Parks Tau. The agreement could reduce or eliminate duties on certain goods, simplifying mutual trade.

item.title: EAEU Sets Preferential Meat Import Quotas for Kyrgyzstan Through 2027
item.description: The Eurasian Economic Commission has established preferential tariff quotas for Kyrgyzstan's meat imports for 2027, totaling 65,000 tons. This includes 58,000 tons for poultry, 5,000 tons for beef, and 2,000 tons for pork. The quotas aim to ensure food security and meet domestic demand.

item.title: Uzbekistan resumes gold exports in July, reaching $1.3 billion
item.description: Uzbekistan has resumed gold exports in July after a pause, shipping $1.3 billion worth of the precious metal, according to preliminary data from the National Statistics Committee. Total foreign trade turnover grew 8.1% year-on-year to $49.5 billion in January-July.

item.title: Housing Renovation to Begin in Three Tashkent Districts Under New Regulations
item.description: Tashkent's mayor has approved measures for complex construction and renovation projects, effective March 1, 2026, through March 1, 2028. A special legal regime will apply to designated land plots. Toshkent Invest has been appointed as the responsible organization, with the Reconstruction and Development Fund providing loans to investment companies.

item.title: Bulat Utemuratov's Foundation Supports Almaty Gasification Project with 460 Million Tenge
item.description: The Bulat Utemuratov Foundation has provided 460 million tenge in charitable aid for Almaty's socially significant gasification project, aiming to connect private homes to natural gas. The project, implemented in collaboration with the Almaty Akimat, includes comprehensive support for residents transitioning from coal to gas heating.
